items.note: The page puts together the factorization, the reduction modulo q^b, the O(V) triangular transformations and the one-interchange realisation of each one of Pi into the claim of exactly a interchanges plus O(V) work, following the proof of Lemma lem:matrix-shear.

items.note: The page gives the paper's procedure: topmost nonzero row, rightmost entry, right multiplication clearing to the left, left multiplication clearing below, scale, delete and repeat. It never says why choosing the topmost row and rightmost entry keeps every operation lower triangular, and the assignment asked for exactly that to be spelled out.

items.note: The lemma's hypotheses are set out: fixed finite set, fixed odd prime q, fields mod q^b, H before D. The conclusion is reached by the later sections. The two closing clauses of the lemma statement are left out, although the interchange (H_i,D_j) shown does pair an H field with a D field.

items.note: The page explains why the choice works: 'A fraction whose denominator is not divisible by q is meaningful modulo q^b', reduction preserves sums and products, and 'A triangular matrix is invertible exactly when its diagonal entries are units'. This is the paper's reasoning in more detail.

Matches the paper. Coordinates are updated in descending physical order, and each 'becomes its diagonal unit times itself plus a fixed combination of earlier coordinates, which still hold their original values'. It cites the controlled-shift lemma with m fixed and notes that inverses are lower triangular.
Gives the paper's order of operations and checks it: 'The net effect on H is E_1(E_1^{-1}H+Pi E_2 D)=H+AD, and D is restored'. The check is correct.

Gives the paper's three-step sequence and the remark that the target follows the control. It checks the sequence on a numerical instance, (5,3)->(5,8)->(8,5)->(8,3), which is correct and plainly works in general; there is no symbolic (h,d)->(h+d,d) check.
'one interchange per one of Pi, and Pi has a ones, so exactly a interchanges'. Temporary tapes are covered by putting all other operations in the O(V) further work, as the paper does.

errors.quote: Any prime larger than all nonzero numerators and denominators in the table works.
errors.problem: The paper says 'a prime exceeding the absolute values of all its nonzero numerators and denominators'. Without absolute values the claim fails for negative numerators: a numerator -7 is exceeded by q=7, which divides it.

errors.quote: The first and last updates target a later field controlled by an earlier one, so they are controlled shifts.
errors.problem: The last update, D_j <- H_i - D_j, is not a pure controlled shift y -> y + a(controls). It also needs the unit scaling y -> -y (negation), which the paper's Lemma 'Controlled shifts and fixed rational scalings' covers separately. The paper says only that both updates target a later field controlled by an earlier one.
